brief: Six habits that decide whether a brand holds together

slots.eyebrow: Consistency is a system, not a preference
slots.subtitle: Six decisions that keep a brand recognisable once other people start using it without you.

slots.title: Components beat
slots.body: A guideline that has to be read gets ignored. A component that has to be used gets used, which is the entire mechanism of consistency at scale.

slots.title: A logo that needs a minimum size
slots.titleAccent: is a logo that will break
slots.body: It will be applied at fourteen pixels and on a two-metre banner by people who have never met you. Both have to work without supervision.

slots.title: Colour discipline does more
slots.body: A consistent grade across mediocre photography reads as a brand. Beautiful photography in five different grades reads as a stock library.

slots.title: The website is the only asset
slots.body: It deserves the same scrutiny as the mark and usually gets a fraction of it, because it feels like a template rather than an identity decision.

slots.title: Guidelines nobody can find
slots.body: The document matters far less than the fact that it is one link, current, and short enough that somebody in a hurry will actually read it.

slots.title: Consistency makes work
slots.body: A perfectly applied system produces mediocre work at speed. These decisions remove friction; they cannot supply the thing worth being consistent about.
Every extra tool is another place the brand drifts. Pick the ones that own a job each, and delete the rest without ceremony.
